conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-01.question: In Psalm 23:2, the Lord leads David beside the still waters.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-01.learningObjective: Observe the shepherd's concrete care in Psalm 23.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says it: he leads beside the still waters, as a shepherd does with his sheep.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Psalm 23:2: he leads me beside the still waters.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-01.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-02.question: In Psalm 23:1, tap whom David calls his shepherd.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-02.learningObjective: Identify the Lord as the shepherd of the psalm.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-02.feedbackCorrect: David begins with God's name: it is the Lord who cares for him as a shepherd.

feedbackWrong.a: "Nada" (nothing) speaks of what will not be lacking, not of who cares.
feedbackWrong.b: "Meu pastor" (my shepherd) is the title David gives; tap the one who receives it.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-02.hint: Look for who comes before the title at the start of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-03.question: According to Psalm 23:4, what comforts David in the valley?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-03.learningObjective: Observe what brings David comfort in the valley.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-03.feedbackCorrect: Rod and staff are a shepherd's tools to guide and protect; they comfort David.

feedbackWrong.b: There are no other shepherds in the psalm: "tu estás comigo".
feedbackWrong.c: David does not speak of his own strength; the comfort comes from what is the Lord's.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not speak of a lamp; it speaks of the rod and the staff.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-03.hint: Read the end of the verse.

options.c: The strength of his own arm
options.d: The light of a lamp on the way

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-04.question: Put Psalm 23:5 in the order of the text.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-04.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: a feast, oil on the head, and an overflowing cup.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the feast; the overflowing cup closes the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-04.hint: The verse begins with the table.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-05.question: In Psalm 23:2, where does the Lord make David lie down?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-05.learningObjective: Remember the concrete image of the shepherd's care.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-05.feedbackCorrect: "Pastos verdejantes" (green pastures): food and rest, chosen by the shepherd.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not take the sheep up high; it speaks of a green place to rest.
feedbackWrong.b: It seems close, but the text speaks of the place where sheep eat.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-05.hint: Think of the place where sheep eat.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-06.question: What does Psalm 23:1 communicate that connects to this context?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-06.learningObjective: Connect David's experience with sheep to the image of the Lord as shepherd.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-06.feedbackCorrect: The former shepherd now sees himself as a sheep: the Lord does for him what he did for the flock.

feedbackWrong.a: Here the shepherd is the Lord; David places himself as a sheep.
feedbackWrong.c: The psalm does not look to David's past; it speaks of who cares for him now.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-06.hint: See who takes the shepherd's place in the verse.

options.a: David sees himself as the shepherd
options.b: David sees a shepherd in the Lord

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-01.question: In Psalm 23:4, David stops being afraid because the Lord takes him out of the valley of the shadow of death.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-01.learningObjective: Understand the reason for David's courage in the valley.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-01.feedbackCorrect: David still walks through the valley; he does not fear because the Lord is with him there.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread: "Ainda que eu ande pelo vale". The reason is another: "porque tu estás comigo".

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-01.hint: See what comes after "não temerei mal nenhum" (I will fear no evil).

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-02.question: In Psalm 23:4, tap the word that introduces the reason David does not fear.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-02.learningObjective: Recognize the cause marker in the text.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-02.feedbackCorrect: "Porque" (for) opens the reason: the Lord is with him, and that is enough in the valley.

feedbackWrong.a: "Mal nenhum" (no evil) says what David does not fear, not why.
feedbackWrong.b: "Ainda que" (even though) admits the valley's danger; the reason for courage comes later.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-02.hint: Look for the word that links the courage to its reason.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-03.question: How do the two parts of Psalm 23:1 connect?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-03.learningObjective: Relate the shepherd to lacking nothing.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-03.feedbackCorrect: The first sentence supports the second: because the Lord is shepherd, nothing will be lacking.

feedbackWrong.a: It is the other way around: the shepherd comes first, and so nothing is lacking.
feedbackWrong.b: The psalm does not speak of David's achievements, but of the Lord's care.
feedbackWrong.d: David makes no promise; he trusts in what the shepherd will give.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-03.hint: Think about which sentence depends on the other.

options.a: Lacking nothing is the condition for the Lord to be shepherd
options.b: David describes the riches he has already gained
options.c: Having the Lord as shepherd is the reason nothing is lacking
options.d: David promises never to ask the Lord for anything

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-04.question: How does the Lord's care move forward in Psalm 23?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-04.feedbackCorrect: From pasture to valley and from valley to table: the Lord cares at every part of the way.

feedbackWrong.default: The psalm starts in the pasture, goes through the valley, and ends at the table and the Lord's house.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-04.hint: The psalm ends in the house of the Lord.

options.a: The shepherd gives rest and direction
options.b: The shepherd goes along in the dark valley
options.c: The Lord serves a feast and welcomes him home

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-05.question: In Psalm 23:3, what does the Lord do with David's soul?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-05.learningObjective: Remember the shepherd's action that renews a person.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-05.feedbackCorrect: "Refrigera" means restores strength: the shepherd gives breath back to the weary.

feedbackWrong.b: Keeping appears in other psalms; here the action is renewing the weary soul.
feedbackWrong.c: The psalm does not speak of examining here; it speaks of renewing strength.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-05.hint: It is the action at the start of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-06.question: What links Psalm 23:1 to Isaiah 40:11?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-06.learningObjective: Relate the image of the Lord as shepherd in Psalms and Isaiah.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts the Lord himself is the shepherd who guides and carries the flock.

feedbackWrong.b: Isaiah shows the opposite: he carries the little lambs in his arms.
feedbackWrong.c: In both texts the shepherd is the Lord, not a human king.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-06.hint: Compare who cares for the flock in the two passages.

options.b: God cares only for the strong

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-01.question: Psalm 23 promises that whoever has the Lord as shepherd does not go through dark valleys.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-01.learningObjective: Distinguish the promise of company from a promise of a life without pain.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-01.feedbackCorrect: The psalm speaks of the valley of death's shadow; the promise is the Lord near, not no valleys.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Psalm 23:4: "Ainda que eu ande pelo vale". The valley exists; the Lord is in it.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-01.hint: See how the valley verse begins.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-02.question: In Psalm 23:4, tap the phrase that shows the Lord near, not distant.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that the holy God cares up close.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-02.feedbackCorrect: "Tu estás comigo": in the darkest place, the Lord is not far; he is at David's side.

feedbackWrong.a: The valley is the place of danger, not the Lord's presence.
feedbackWrong.c: "Não temerei" (I will not fear) is David's reaction; the reason lies in the Lord's presence.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-02.hint: Look for a presence, not a place or a feeling.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-03.question: What reading does Psalm 23:1 support about the Lord?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading the text supports about God's care.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-03.feedbackCorrect: "Meu pastor": the Lord is not only everyone's God; he cares for David personally.

feedbackWrong.b: The psalm speaks of the valley of the shadow of death (Ps 23:4); the Lord is in it.
feedbackWrong.c: What is not lacking is the shepherd's care, not every wish David has.
feedbackWrong.d: David calls the Lord "meu pastor": the holy one does not stay far away.

options.a: The Lord cares for David up close, as a shepherd
options.b: With the Lord near, there are no dark valleys
options.c: Whoever has the Lord gets everything they want
options.d: God is too holy to care for anyone up close

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-04.question: Which sequence shows the shepherd thread that runs through Psalm 23:1?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-04.learningObjective: See Psalm 23 as the start of a thread that reaches Jesus.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-04.feedbackCorrect: David's shepherd appears in Jesus, who gives his life, and guides his people to the end.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: David's psalm (Ps 23), Jesus (John 10:11), and the end (Rev 7:17).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-04.hint: Follow the Bible's order: Psalms, Gospels, Revelation.

options.a: David calls the Lord his shepherd
options.b: Jesus, the good Shepherd, gives his life for the sheep
options.c: The Lamb on the throne guides to the springs of life

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-05.question: In Psalm 23:6, what follows David along with goodness?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows the Lord's faithful love.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-05.feedbackCorrect: Mercy is God's faithful love: it does not stay behind, it follows David every day.

feedbackWrong.a: Peace fits the psalm, but it is not the word in the verse.
feedbackWrong.c: Righteousness appears in Psalm 23:3, in the paths; here goodness has another partner.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-05.hint: It is the faithful love that goes with David his whole life.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-06.question: What links Psalm 23:1 to John 10:11?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-06.learningObjective: Connect the shepherd of Psalm 23 to Jesus, as Jesus himself does.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus takes up the image of Psalm 23: he is the shepherd, and he gives his life for the sheep.

feedbackWrong.a: David places himself as a sheep; in John, the one who says "I am the good shepherd" is Jesus.
feedbackWrong.c: John 10 does not speak of church leaders; it speaks of Jesus and his sheep.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-06.hint: See who speaks in the first person in John 10:11.

estudo:entrada-deus-04.context: David tended sheep before he became king. He knew what a shepherd does: leads to pasture and water, guides along the way, and defends from danger. In this psalm, he uses that image to speak of the Lord himself.
estudo:entrada-deus-04.focusQuestion: In what part of your path do you need to remember that the Lord is with you?
estudo:entrada-deus-04.keywordGloss: One who guides, feeds, and protects the sheep; David gives this name to the Lord.
facts: David calls the Lord his shepherd.
The Lord leads David beside the still waters.
In the valley of the shadow of death, David fears no evil.
The Lord's rod and staff bring comfort.
The Lord prepares a feast in front of David's enemies.
Goodness and mercy follow David every day.
